name: Portsea Back Beach
signature: Dramatic cliffs, serious surf, and the wildest coastal scenery at the very tip of the Peninsula
editorNote:
Portsea Back Beach is one of the most spectacular pieces of coastline in Victoria — a narrow beach wedged between dramatic limestone cliffs at the tip of the Peninsula, with Bass Strait swell wrapping in from both directions. It is beautiful, exposed, and not to be underestimated.

The beach is patrolled by Portsea SLSC on weekends and public holidays in summer. Outside patrol hours, the currents and shore break can be genuinely dangerous. The clifftop walk between Portsea Back Beach and London Bridge is one of the Peninsula's best short walks — dramatic views, unusual rock formations, and usually quiet even in peak season.

Combine with the Portsea Hotel for post-beach drinks and the calm front beach for kids who want water without the swell.
whyWeGo: The most dramatic beach setting on the Peninsula — cliffs, surf, and a clifftop walk that most visitors never find.
ifOnlyOneThing: Walk the clifftop track toward London Bridge. Give yourself 45 minutes.
